intent: Escalates a BedrockCommand from this node to another node in the cluster (leader, a named peer, or all peers) over a pooled TCP socket and fills in the command's response.

objects.name: SQLiteClusterMessenger
objects.role: opens/reuses a socket to a peer, sends a serialized command, and reads back its response

objects.name: SQLiteClusterMessenger::WaitForReadyResult
objects.role: outcome of waiting for a socket to become ready (timeout, disconnect, abort, etc.)

name_fit.note: clearly a messenger between nodes, sits correctly with SQLiteNode/SQLitePeer.

naming_quality.note: two overloaded runOnPeer methods (bool vs. peer-name) have different retry semantics but the same name.

intent: Represents one other node in the cluster as seen from this node: its connection socket, replication state, and the synchronization/standup metadata SQLiteNode needs to run consensus.

objects.name: SQLitePeer
objects.role: one peer's connection + replication/consensus state, guarded by an internal mutex

objects.name: SQLitePeer::Response
objects.role: a peer's vote on a standup request (NONE/APPROVE/DENY)

objects.name: SQLitePeer::PeerPostPollStatus
objects.role: result of postPoll: OK, just-connected, socket error, or socket closed

objects.name: operator<<(ostream&, atomic<SQLitePeer::Response>&)
objects.role: streams a Response's name

misfits.why: claims 'see friend class declaration above' but no friend is declared anywhere in this file - a stale/incorrect cross-reference left over from an earlier version

name_fit.note: does exactly what the name says.

naming_quality.note: consistent S-prefix and trailing-underscore constructor params; the stale friend-class comment is a minor documentation defect.

intent: Hands out SQLite database handles to worker threads from a bounded pool, creating new handles lazily up to a max and blocking callers when it's exhausted.

objects.name: SQLitePool
objects.role: bounded pool of SQLite handles cloned from one base handle; get/initialize/return an index

objects.name: SQLiteScopedHandle
objects.role: RAII wrapper that returns its pool index to the pool when it goes out of scope

naming_quality.note: consistent with repo convention; getIndex returns a bare size_t rather than a typed token, so any size_t can be passed to returnToPool.

intent: Base representation of a command as it moves through the cluster: wire-format request/response, a cross-node id, completion flag, and escalation timing; BedrockCommand builds on top of it.

objects.name: SQLiteCommand
objects.role: holds request/response/id/timing for a command; move-only via a private backing field for the const `request` reference

objects.name: SQLiteCommand::preprocessRequest
objects.role: assigns a requestID and warns on deprecated commandExecuteTime, run before `request` is bound

misfits.why: deprecation-specific handling of one legacy wire field living inside an otherwise generic request-preprocessing helper

location_fit.note: correctly the base type alongside the rest of sqlitecluster.

naming_quality.note: private backing field is named `privateRequest` instead of the repo's usual `_` prefix (e.g. `_request`), inconsistent with the rest of the codebase's own convention.

intent: Wraps commit/rollback of a SQLite database with the cluster-aware checks needed to do so safely: only commit while still leader, and run an optional plugin-notification hook during prepare.

objects.name: SQLiteCore
objects.role: commits or rolls back a transaction on a wrapped SQLite&, refusing to commit if the node is no longer leading

name_fit.note: "Core" is a bit generic but the content (commit/rollback gating) is coherent and singular.

naming_quality.note: notificationHandler's function-pointer parameter is named `_db`, echoing the class's own `_db` member despite being an unrelated parameter.

intent: Generates a random, table-unique int64 ID for use as a primary key.

objects.name: SQLiteUtils
objects.role: static-only helper; getRandomID picks a random ID and retries until it's not already present in the given table/column

name_fit.note: "Utils" is generic for a single-function class, though the single function itself is coherent.

location_fit.note: SQLite-specific ID generation belongs in sqlitecluster.

naming_quality.note: fine as far as it goes; a one-function Utils class invites unrelated helpers to accrete.

intent: Abstract interface a SQLiteNode uses to call back into whatever server embeds it: login notifications, state-change notifications to plugins, and command-port blocking.

objects.name: SQLiteServer
objects.role: pure-virtual interface (onNodeLogin, notifyStateChangeToPlugins, blockCommandPort, unblockCommandPort), extends STCPManager

location_fit.note: the callback contract for SQLiteNode's host server belongs here.
